angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 997,980.4 km at 263.18 pc = 0.051 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is published; the disc is far too small to resolve.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 3.7996 +/- 0.0104 mas (photometry/gaia-dr3-source.csv), no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius: 10^0.1567 = 1.4345 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius, the log10 stellar radius of Evans-Soma et al. (2025), Nature Astronomy, 'SiO and a super-stellar C/O ratio in the atmosphere of the giant exoplanet WASP-121b' (arXiv:2506.01771), Supplementary Table 1 (white phase-curve fit, best-fit column), the fit whose planet maps this system shows (derived R* 1.434). GM from the same fit's stellar mass, 1.332 solar masses, times the JPL solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2. Their isochrone analysis (Supplementary Table 9) gives 1.49 solar radii and 1.36 solar masses. presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the star's spin axis is measured only through the planet's nearly polar orbit (Bourrier et al. 2020).
effectiveTemperatureSource: Evans-Soma et al. (2025), Nature Astronomy, Supplementary Table 9: 6,481 K from their spectroscopic and isochrone analysis (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01771)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json), because no image of the photosphere exists (see investigations.json).
